subject: Request: hosted API penetration test report & secure delivery options
body:
Message 1 (oldest)
From: Jared Lee <jared.lee@fintechcorp.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@fintechcorp.com
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: latest penetration test for Hosted API

Hi Hannah / Monica,

We are updating our vendor security review for the upcoming integration and need the most recent penetration test report for Redwood's Hosted API. Specifically: 
- The full (redacted as needed) PT report, or a secure way to retrieve it.
- Scope of the assessment (which surfaces / customer-facing endpoints, whether authentication/authorization flows and logging were in-scope).
- Whether customer data or live customer environments were used during testing.
- Current remediation status for any findings that were classified as High / Critical, and expected ETA for outstanding items.

We cannot accept reports that are emailed insecurely. Please advise secure transfer options (S3 presign, virtual data room, NDAs needed, etc.), and any hoops we need to jump through on our side.

Thanks,
Jared Lee
Security Engineer, FinTechCorp
security@fintechcorp.com

---

Message 2
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Jared Lee <jared.lee@fintechcorp.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: latest penetration test for Hosted API

Hi Jared — thanks for the request. Short answer: we can provide a redacted copy of the full penetration test report for Redwood's Hosted API under a mutual NDA or via a time-limited, authenticated download. Options we commonly offer: 

1) Redacted PDF via secure S3 presigned URL (recommended): we generate a presigned link with strict IP/expiry controls (typically 7 days).
2) Virtual data room (ShareFile / Box / secure Drive) — for larger exchanges / multiple artifacts.
3) In some highly sensitive cases we arrange a read-only session with our security team (screen-share + recorded access).

Scope summary (from the Jan 2026 assessment):
- Surface: public Hosted API endpoints (text generation, embeddings, chat endpoints), auth flows (API keys and token management), and infra orchestration components that serve hosted customers.
- Excluded: customer-hosted private deployments (VPC/on-prem packages) and partner integrations by default (unless explicitly requested).
- Test model: credentialed blackbox + authenticated API fuzzing, and targeted authenticated tests against token issuance and KV caches. No live customer data was accessed or used as part of testing.

We have a short executive summary PDF attached (Redwood_PT_Report_REDACTED_2026-01.pdf). For the detailed report we will need a signed mutual NDA or confirmation you accept access via our presigned link process. If you prefer the NDA route, we can send our standard vendor NDA for signature.

Possible next steps:
- If presign is OK: confirm the primary recipient email (for audit) and your preferred expiry (we default to 7 days).
- If NDA: say so and I will loop in legal.

Regards,
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Customer Security (acting)
Redwood Inference
hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai

Attachment: Redwood_PT_Report_REDACTED_2026-01.pdf (redacted summary, 3 pages)

---

Message 3
From: Jared Lee <jared.lee@fintechcorp.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@fintechcorp.com
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 08:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: latest penetration test for Hosted API

Hi Hannah,

Thanks for the summary — presign would be fine. Please presign to jared.lee@fintechcorp.com. A couple of clarifying items from our side: 
- We saw a reference to an authenticated fuzzing test. Are there any open High / Critical findings related to auth (token issuance, API key leakage, or misconfigured CORS) remaining? If so, can you provide the remediation ETA and whether any mitigations are in place in the published runtime?
- We need to include evidence of remediation for any High findings in our vendor file. A JIRA or ticket reference would be helpful.

If you can include the presigned link and any ticket refs, that should be fine — NDA would be slower for us.

Appreciate it,
Jared

---

Message 4
From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Jared Lee <jared.lee@fintechcorp.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 14:00:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: latest penetration test for Hosted API

Hi Jared — Dev from infra/security here, following up with remediation specifics. Per the Jan 2026 pen test: 
- One High finding: improper token invalidation window in our older key-rotation path (affects token refresh flow for long-lived keys). Ticket: INF-3421 (https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-3421). Status: remediation completed and deployed to Hosted API on 2026-01-25. Mitigation: rotation logic tightened, additional checks added to token revocation path, and regressions covered by unit + integration tests.
- One Medium finding: overly permissive CORS on an internal admin endpoint — fix deployed 2026-01-18; ACL tightened and endpoint removed from public routable config. Ticket: INF-3389.
- No Critical findings were raised.

We will publish the presigned URL to jared.lee@fintechcorp.com now. Notes on the artifact: the full report remains redacted for customer-identifying data and internal IP addresses; the remediation evidence section contains ticket refs and deployment timestamps.

Presigned link (attached as a short stub file in this thread for audit): https://s3-presign.redwood.example/abc123 (expires 2026-02-18T14:00:00Z)

Attachment: redwood_pt_presign_link.txt (contains presigned URL, expiry, and access audit id)

If you need signed attestations or a compliance pack (SOC 2 type II report + accompanying control matrix), we can coordinate a joint handoff with our compliance team — let me know.

Thanks,
Dev Patel
Senior Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
dev.patel@redwood.ai

---

Message 5 (newest)
From: Jared Lee <jared.lee@fintechcorp.com>
To: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@fintechcorp.com
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 15:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: latest penetration test for Hosted API

Dev / Hannah — received the presigned link and the summary PDF, downloaded successfully. Confirming:
- Ticket INF-3421 and INF-3389 match our expectations and include timestamps that demonstrate remediation is in prod.
- The redactions are acceptable for our vendor file.

Can we schedule a 30-min sync next week to walk through the remediation evidence and the control mapping to SOC 2 sections relevant to auth and incident response? I can bring our technical reviewer.

Prefer Wednesday (Feb 18) afternoon PST if that works for you.

Thanks again — Jared
Security Engineer, FinTechCorp
